consequence.statement: For packages stored in private repositories, package.yaml can now be extracted — a capability that was not available before this release; the evidence states no failure, rejection, or required migration.
consequence.remediation: No action required; environments that use private package repositories can verify that package.yaml extraction (and package installation from those repositories) now works as expected.

original.statement: Crossplane 2.0.0 enables extracting package.yaml from private repositories.

consequence.statement: Nothing breaks or changes for an operator who does nothing: the `crossplane xpkg extract` CLI command now uses default auth when fetching from a remote registry, so it can also read packages in private repositories. In-cluster package installation is not affected.

corrected.statement: Crossplane 2.0.0 adds default registry authentication to the `crossplane xpkg extract` CLI command, so it can extract package.yaml from private repositories; this is an additive CLI capability with no operational consequence for operators who do nothing.

decision.reason: The linked PR [ev-fce5b51d8226] says the change "adds default auth for `crossplane xpkg extract` when fetching from a remote registry, to support private repositories", and it changes only one file, cmd/crank/xpkg/extract.go [ev-550788c9f271]. So this is a new capability in the CLI command, not a change to package installation or to anything running in a cluster. The release note [ev-a599a29bbeba] and the PR give no sign that existing behaviour changes, fails or needs a migration. An operator who does nothing has no operational consequence, so the kind should be none (informational), not behavior-change; the proposed remediation also wrongly brings in package installation.
